1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)
43: 
44: **Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
45: **Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
46: integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.
47: 
48: ### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process
49: 
50: **Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
51: `packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
52: **Builds:**
53: 
54: - **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
55:   `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
56:   `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
57: - The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
58:   inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
59:   skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
60: - SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
61: - Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
62: - The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).
63: 
64: **Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
65: fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
66: `not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.

68: ### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI
69: 
70: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.

82: 
83: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
84: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.

87: breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,

91: resume-run action, and export.

94: 
95: ### WS4 — Settings, app shell & packaging
96: 
97: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/**`,
98: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/ui/**` (shared controls),
99: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/settings*.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/theme.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/router.tsx`,
100: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
101: **State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
102: Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
103: `Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
104: **Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
105: `settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
106: **Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
107: demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.
108: 
109: ### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)
110: 
111: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
112: **Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
113: from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
114: passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
115: ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
116: Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
117: findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
118: synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
119: **Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.
120: 
121: ### WS6 — Research block
122: 
123: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
124: **Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
125: segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
126: `ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
127: and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
128: allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
129: (`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
130: **Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.
131: 
132: ### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car
133: 
134: **Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
135: `packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
136: **Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
137: skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
138: findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
139: route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
140: **Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
141: `formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
142: uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
143: to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
144: **Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
145: outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.
146: 
147: ### WS8 — Prioritization
148: 
149: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.
150: **Builds:** explainable scoring used by the AI Splitter's priority mode. Factors are computed
151: deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence
152: strength from independent sources × reliability and evidence level; competitive gap from
153: `competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only
154: where a judgement is needed (brand fit, ease), always with a one-line note. It uses `weightedTotal`
155: and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers. It also flags
156: "high score, weak evidence".
157: **Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
158: expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

169: type InvokeKeys<T> = {
170:   [K in keyof T]: T[K] extends (...args: never[]) => Promise<unknown> ? K : never;
171: }[keyof T];

173: /** What main must implement: every request/response method (event subscriptions excluded). */
174: export type ReqflowHandlers = {
175:   [N in keyof ReqflowApi]: Pick<ReqflowApi[N], InvokeKeys<ReqflowApi[N]>>;
176: };
177: 
178: /** Every request/response method, by namespace. Preload allow-lists exactly these channels. */
179: export const IPC_INVOKE_METHODS = {
180:   app: ["info"],
181:   templates: ["list"],
182:   blocks: ["preview"],
183:   workflows: ["list", "get", "save", "remove"],
184:   files: ["import"],
185:   runs: ["start", "get", "list", "blockOutput", "resume", "cancel"],
186:   requirements: ["list", "get", "edit", "decide", "reset"],
187:   audit: ["list"],

189:   reasoning: ["forRun", "latest", "forRequirement"],
190:   exports: ["requirements"],
191: } as const satisfies { [N in keyof ReqflowApi]: readonly InvokeKeys<ReqflowApi[N]>[] };

194: type Listed = { [N in keyof ReqflowApi]: (typeof IPC_INVOKE_METHODS)[N][number] };
195: type Unlisted = {
196:   [N in keyof ReqflowApi]: Exclude<InvokeKeys<ReqflowApi[N]>, Listed[N]>;
197: }[keyof ReqflowApi];

202: export function ipcChannel(namespace: string, method: string): string {

204: }

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements

  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a

1: import { z } from "zod";
2: import { Finding, Theme } from "./finding";
3: import { Requirement } from "./requirement";
4: import { Source, SourceRecord } from "./source";
5: 
6: /**
7:  * The single envelope that flows along every workflow edge (n8n-style: one input, one output).
8:  * A node reads the keys it `consumes` and returns the envelope with the keys it `produces` updated.
9:  */
10: export const DATA_KEYS = ["sources", "records", "findings", "themes", "requirements"] as const;
11: export const DataKey = z.enum(DATA_KEYS);
12: export type DataKey = z.infer<typeof DataKey>;
13: 
14: export const PipelineData = z.object({
15:   sources: z.array(Source),
16:   records: z.array(SourceRecord),
17:   findings: z.array(Finding),
18:   themes: z.array(Theme),
19:   requirements: z.array(Requirement),
20: });
21: export type PipelineData = z.infer<typeof PipelineData>;
22: 
23: export function emptyPipelineData(): PipelineData {
24:   return { sources: [], records: [], findings: [], themes: [], requirements: [] };
25: }
26: 
27: function mergeById<T extends { id: string }>(lists: T[][]): T[] {
28:   const byId = new Map<string, T>();
29:   for (const list of lists) for (const item of list) byId.set(item.id, item);
30:   return [...byId.values()];
31: }
32: 
33: /**
34:  * How the engine combines several incoming edges into one node input:
35:  * concatenate per key and de-duplicate by `id`; a later input wins (order = edge order),
36:  * first-seen position is kept so output order stays stable.
37:  */
38: export function mergePipelineData(...parts: PipelineData[]): PipelineData {
39:   return {
40:     sources: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.sources)),
41:     records: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.records)),
42:     findings: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.findings)),
43:     themes: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.themes)),
44:     requirements: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.requirements)),
45:   };
46: }
47: 
48: export function countPipelineData(data: PipelineData): Record<DataKey, number> {
49:   return {
50:     sources: data.sources.length,
51:     records: data.records.length,
52:     findings: data.findings.length,
53:     themes: data.themes.length,
54:     requirements: data.requirements.length,
55:   };

1: # HIL Report Design
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: The HIL (Human In The Loop) sample PDF report provides an exported, point-in-time snapshot of selected data samples at a review gate, facilitating cross-functional communication and upstream concept validation before committing to final requirements.
6: 
7: ## Theoretical Foundations
8: 
9: 1. **Cross-functional Communication**
10:    _Ding 2025 DOI 10.38007/IJSSEM.2025.060218_ highlights the critical importance of cross-functional communication. The HIL PDF report surfaces specific excerpts, rationales, and themes out of the AI pipeline to non-technical stakeholders (e.g., engineering, marketing) in a format that does not require app installation or system access, fostering shared understanding.
11: 
12: 2. **Universal Scoring and Prioritization Limits**
13:    _Santos et al 2019 DOI 10.1590/0103-6513.20180108_ notes in a survey of 72 Brazilian firms that while prioritization methods exist, associations are not causal and there is no universal scoring mechanism. The report explicitly documents prioritization rationales and handles conflicting evidence without assuming the AI's score is an absolute truth. The PM makes the final call based on the sample evidence.
14: 
15: 3. **Early Problem Solving & Concurrent Engineering**
16:    _Midler/Navarre 2004 Wiley Guide pp1368-1388_ advocates for concurrent engineering and early problem solving. The HIL report's upstream concept validation and learning—separate from product commitment—enables teams to identify gaps (weak evidence, conflicting findings) before locking in targets. The export strictly represents a sample snapshot, not a final approval.
17: 
18: ## Design Limitations
19: 
20: - **No Gantt/CPM/PERT:** The report mapping focuses on data lineage and rationale rather than task dependencies or durations. Requirements definition in this context is about features and value, not project scheduling.
21: - **Future Enhancements:** Currently, optional action notes (owner, objective) are only embedded in the PDF. Persisting these owners/review records back into the audit trail or pipeline state would require a contract change in a future iteration.
22: 
23: ## Security & Architecture
24: 
25: - **No External Assets or Scripts:** The HTML template generated for the PDF is entirely self-contained. A Content-Security-Policy (CSP) is embedded to deny external network requests and inline scripts (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline';`).
26: - **Hidden BrowserWindow:** The PDF generation happens within a hidden, strictly-sandboxed Electron `BrowserWindow` with JavaScript disabled to prevent arbitrary code execution across the IPC bridge.

10:   constructor(
11:     readonly code: string,
12:     message: string,
13:     readonly details?: unknown,

15:     super(message);

17:   }

20: type InvokeClient = {
21:   [N in keyof typeof IPC_INVOKE_METHODS]: {
22:     [M in (typeof IPC_INVOKE_METHODS)[N][number]]: M extends keyof ReqflowApi[N]
23:       ? ReqflowApi[N][M]
24:       : never;
25:   };
26: };
27: 
28: /** Builds the typed API from the bridge; a method missing from IPC_INVOKE_METHODS is a type error here. */
29: export function createApi(bridge: ReqflowBridge): ReqflowApi {
30:   const client = Object.fromEntries(
31:     Object.entries(IPC_INVOKE_METHODS).map(([ns, methods]) => [
32:       ns,
33:       Object.fromEntries(
34:         methods.map((method) => [
35:           method,
36:           async (...args: unknown[]) => {
37:             const result = await bridge.invoke(ipcChannel(ns, method), ...args);
38:             if (!result.ok) {
39:               throw new ReqflowError(result.error.code, result.error.message, result.error.details);
40:             }
41:             return result.value;
42:           },
43:         ]),
44:       ),
45:     ]),
46:   ) as InvokeClient;
47:   return { ...client, runs: { ...client.runs, onUpdate: bridge.onRunUpdate } };

+# HIL Format-Check Report
+
+## Usage
+
+Open a HIL review report, choose the data step to inspect, expand **Format-check PDF**,
+and select the points to include. The defaults are the first three items in each dataset,
+with a combined maximum of 15. Each dataset shows its first 50 candidates in source order;
+this is purposeful format inspection, not representative statistical sampling.
+
+Optional objective, owner/consulted functions, checkpoint and validation-action notes are
+human-authored and report-only. **Export sample PDF** opens the native save dialog. Cancel
+does not generate a file. Errors remain visible. Nothing is sent to a network service.
+
+Saved runs use their frozen graph, scope and stored data; a source preview is explicitly
+labelled as a live preview, not a saved run or review record. The PDF identifies the sampled
+step separately from the HIL gate. Export never checks the review checkbox, resumes a run,
+changes a requirement status or creates a reviewer signature.
+
+## Management Improvements
+
+The report is structured as a decision brief, not a data dump:
+
+- A management brief exposes selected candidates, status, priority, score and evidence level.
+- Review attention flags missing targets, weak/assumption-led evidence, conflicting findings,
+  unselected references, missing priority rationale and recorded uncertainties.
+- Human action notes encourage explicit ownership, cross-functional consultation and a next
+  validation checkpoint without inventing dates or assignments.
+- Full counts, selected counts and omission counts make the scope of inspection auditable.
+- Upstream lineage includes nested workplace paths and routed port labels, but no block
+  parameters, connection strings or runtime logs.
+- Selected requirements include targets/acceptance, factor values/weights/notes, rationale,
+  assumptions, uncertainties and supporting/conflicting IDs.
+- Selected findings retain verbatim excerpts and source/record locators. Selected records
+  retain original text and structured columns so the reviewer can check their format.
+- Sources provide reliability, publisher, retrieval/publication dates and URI for traceability.
+  Unselected references explicitly remain omitted instead of being expanded silently.
+
+Absence from the PDF is not absence from the complete dataset. The sample cannot establish
+decision readiness or be used as a substitute for full evidence review in ReqFlow. PDFs
+can contain confidential excerpts; sharing must be limited to authorized reviewers.
+
+## Research Basis
+
+The three papers supplied by the user were reviewed as design input, not imported as
+customer evidence or treated as an automatic prioritization policy.
+
+### Cross-Functional Communication
+
+Junchun Ding (2025), *Cross-Functional Team Collaboration and Project Management in the
+Automotive Industry*, pp. 162-170, DOI
+[10.38007/IJSSEM.2025.060218](https://doi.org/10.38007/IJSSEM.2025.060218).
+
+Sections 2-4 emphasize information handoffs, shared goals, inter-departmental conflicts and
+short feedback cycles. This motivates a common brief with lineage, specific validation
+questions and named consulted functions. The paper's illustrative efficiency formulas and
+examples are not used as validated BMW performance metrics.
+
+### People, Change and Governance
+
+Santos, Barriga, Jugend and Cauchick-Miguel (2019), *Organizational factors influencing
+project success: an assessment in the automotive industry*, Production 29, e20180108, DOI
+[10.1590/0103-6513.20180108](https://doi.org/10.1590/0103-6513.20180108).
+
+The survey of 72 Brazilian automotive companies associates project success with organizational
+culture, change management, top-management support, training and communication. The report
+therefore foregrounds understandable rationale, explicit uncertainties and human next actions,
+not just score totals. Single respondents, geographic/sample limits and model adjustment
+limit generalization. These associations do not prove causation and should not become
+universal scoring weights or project-success predictions.
+
+### Concurrent Engineering and Learning
+
+Christophe Midler and Christian Navarre (2004), *Project Management in the Automotive
+Industry*, chapter 55, *The Wiley Guide to Managing Projects*, pp. 1368-1388.
+
+Pages 1375-1377 discuss accountability and early involvement of specialist functions;
+pages 1381-1382 distinguish upstream concept validation and acquired knowledge from product
+launch commitments. Pages 1384-1385 highlight interfaces and negotiated compromises. This
+motivates early conflict/gap visibility, a cross-functional checkpoint, and a clear distinction
+between inspecting a sample, learning from evidence and approving a product requirement.
+The chapter is historical; its timelines and performance benchmarks are not current BMW targets.
+
+## Deliberate Limits and Next Steps
+
+- Gantt, CPM and PERT require actual tasks, dependencies and duration estimates. ReqFlow does
+  not have those inputs; a data lineage diagram is not a schedule or critical-path analysis.
+- PDF action notes are not persisted assignments. A future review-action contract could store
+  owner, due checkpoint, validation method, stakeholder response and escalation status.
+- A future review record should capture reviewer identity/role, rationale, evidence version,
+  change since the previous gate and closure of open questions. Existing HIL pause/resume
+  events are not independent multi-reviewer signatures.
+- Later exploration/commitment readiness should distinguish customer-value validation from
+  feature feasibility and platform interfaces, while keeping engineering specs, regulatory
+  topics and pricing/business cases outside this prototype's scope.
+
+## Implementation and Verification
+
+`exports.hilReport` is the typed, allowlisted IPC method. Main validates the request with
+core Zod schemas: bounded metadata, unique sample IDs, nonnegative integer counts, valid
+lineage references and 1-15 selected points. Samples over 2 MB are rejected explicitly,
+never silently truncated. No arbitrary HTML is accepted from the renderer.
+
+Main generates escaped HTML with no scripts or external assets and a restrictive CSP.
+A hidden, sandboxed Electron window with JavaScript and Node disabled prints A4 PDF and
+is destroyed on success, failure or a 15-second timeout. Native save, rendering and disk
+errors propagate to the UI. No PDF library or external dependency is added.
+
+Colocated tests cover validation, omissions, escaping, verbatim fields, reference gaps,
+selection limits, cancellation, save/render/write failures, and window cleanup/security.
+Desktop smoke exercises checkbox deselection, actual IPC/PDF generation and PDF signature,
+and captures the expanded/saved report at desktop and minimum supported window sizes.
*** End Patch

1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)
43: 
44: **Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
45: **Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
46: integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.
47: 
48: ### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process
49: 
50: **Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
51: `packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
52: **Builds:**
53: 
54: - **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
55:   `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
56:   `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
57: - The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
58:   inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
59:   skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
60: - SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
61: - Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
62: - The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).
63: 
64: **Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
65: fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
66: `not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.
67: 
68: ### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI
69: 
70: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.
71: **State today:** palette, workplace (React Flow), blocks with ports, connect with validation, inspector
72: with parameter forms, inner workplaces with breadcrumb, delete with confirmation, snap/minimap from
73: Settings. The flow lives in memory (`components/dataflow/store.ts`).
74: **Builds next:** save/load (`api.workflows.*`, autosave), "New from template" (`api.templates.list()`),
75: undo/redo, copy/paste, a Run button with live status, counts and logs on each block

78: **Done when:** you can build the default template by hand, save it, reload it, and see run states on the
79: blocks (mocked until WS1 lands).

81: ### WS3 — Car tab: requirements review & audit UI
82: 
83: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
84: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.
85: **Builds:** the Car tab as the output page: the car (keep the car visual) with its requirements as a
86: list or board, grouped by ranking, with filters and sorting. A detail view shows targets, a score
87: breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
88: uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
89: Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing
90: with rationale, a History view, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a
91: resume-run action, and export.
92: **Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
93: and the decision and edit flows call `api.requirements.*`.
94: 
95: ### WS4 — Settings, app shell & packaging
96: 
97: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/**`,
98: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/ui/**` (shared controls),

100: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
101: **State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
102: Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
103: `Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
104: **Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
105: `settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
106: **Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
107: demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.
108: 
109: ### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)
110: 
111: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
112: **Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
113: from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
114: passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
115: ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
116: Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
117: findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
118: synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
119: **Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.
120: 
121: ### WS6 — Research block
122: 
123: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
124: **Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
125: segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
126: `ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
127: and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
128: allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
129: (`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
130: **Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.
131: 
132: ### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car
133: 
134: **Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
135: `packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
136: **Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
137: skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
138: findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
139: route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
140: **Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
141: `formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
142: uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
143: to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
144: **Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
145: outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.
146: 
147: ### WS8 — Prioritization
148: 
149: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.
150: **Builds:** explainable scoring used by the AI Splitter's priority mode. Factors are computed
151: deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence
152: strength from independent sources × reliability and evidence level; competitive gap from
153: `competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only
154: where a judgement is needed (brand fit, ease), always with a one-line note. It uses `weightedTotal`
155: and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers. It also flags
156: "high score, weak evidence".
157: **Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
158: expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
   calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
   remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.

9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
   tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
   one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
   starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.

## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)

```
npm install          # once
npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
npm test             # vitest, all packages
npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
npm run format       # prettier
npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
```
